themes_detail.label: Street Signs Damaged Wave
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints spiked to 8 reports this week versus a baseline of 1.1 per week—a 611% increase (z-score: 4.26)—suggesting either vandalism, weather damage, or infrastructure neglect affecting wayfinding and safety in CD 314 this week.
evidence: 8 street sign damage complaints this week vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (611% spike, z-score: 4.26)
High statistical significance indicates sudden onset rather than gradual wear
Timing suggests acute event (weather, construction, or vandalism campaign)
reporting_angles: Canvas neighborhoods to identify whether signs are vandalized, bent, or knocked down by vehicles; photograph hotspots
Interview DOT about maintenance schedules and whether they've received bulk work orders for this district

themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Shortage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket placement complaints jumped to 6 this week from a baseline of 1.4 per week—a 336% increase (z-score: 6.65)—indicating residents are reporting insufficient trash infrastructure on streets and in public spaces across CD 314 this week.
evidence: 6 litter basket placement complaints this week vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (336% spike, z-score: 6.65)
High z-score (6.65) indicates statistically anomalous cluster, not random variation
Timing is concurrent with street sign spike, suggesting possible underlying environmental maintenance gap
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to see if they cluster on specific streets (e.g., near transit hubs, parks, commercial strips)
Interview Sanitation about basket inventory, placement standards, and whether budget cuts or staffing reductions have affected this district

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees & Branches Hazard
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints rose to 14 this week versus a 3.8-per-week baseline—a 273% increase (z-score: 3.53)—suggesting potential safety hazards and visibility issues from unmanicured vegetation across CD 314 this week.
evidence: 14 overgrown tree/branch complaints this week vs. 3.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (273% spike, z-score: 3.53)
Spike timing suggests seasonal growth or deferred Parks Department maintenance
Convergence signal: street signs damaged + litter baskets missing + overgrown trees = possible public space maintenance breakdown
reporting_angles: Visit complaint addresses to assess whether branches are blocking signs, sidewalks, or sightlines; document with photos
Contact Parks Department to determine if this district has deferred maintenance requests or staffing gaps affecting tree care

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Accumulating
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints jumped to 4 this week from a 0.5-per-week baseline—a 700% increase (z-score: 4.04)—indicating a sudden surge in street clutter or potential theft/dumping of bikes across CD 314 this week.
evidence: 4 abandoned bike complaints this week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 4.04)
Sharp z-score (4.04) indicates cluster event rather than baseline noise
Timing correlates with broader public space infrastructure concerns (signs, trash baskets, overgrown trees)
reporting_angles: Visit complaint locations to photograph abandoned bikes and assess condition (salvageable vs. dumped debris)
Interview NYPD about whether bike theft or chop shops in the neighborhood have increased; contact Citi Bike about missing equipment

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Alert (3 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints spiked to 5 three weeks ago versus a 0.8-per-week baseline—a 567% increase (z-score: 6.43)—but this signal is aging and no current-week data confirms persistence; worth monitoring for resurgence.
evidence: 5 air quality complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (567% spike, z-score: 6.43)
Spike is dated; no current-week confirmation of sustained air quality issues
Possible causes: construction dust, vehicle emissions event, or industrial activity (requires investigative followup)
reporting_angles: Check EPA AirNow data and DEP monitors for CD 314 to see if any spike occurred 3 weeks ago; cross-reference with construction permits filed in that window
Interview residents who filed complaints to learn what they observed (dust, smell, visibility) and whether symptoms have returned
